newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Sharon behind plan to ease Israeli PM's ouster.
newsitem.headline: Sharon behind plan to ease Israeli PM's ouster.

text.p: Israel's Ariel Sharon, having lost a bid for more power in government, is rallying disaffected lawmakers behind a plan that would ease Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's ouster.

Netanyahu this month denied Sharon -- the 69-year-old national infrastructure minister and a hawkish former general -- the job of finance minister and a role in shaping negotiating strategy opposite the Palestinians.

Labour opposition legislators Shimon Peres and Moshe Shahal said they discussed with Sharon his proposal to lower to 61 -- from 80 -- the number of members in the 120-seat parliament legally required to oust a prime minister.

"There is no proper decision-making process in the government and consultation (by the prime minister) with ministers who have a contribution to make is almost non-existent," Sharon told Israel Radio.

"But if the prime minister -- and it doesn't matter which prime minister -- knows there is a way for parties and coalition partners to put him in a less comfortable position, I am sure he will want, or have to, consult," Sharon said.

Israel's Haaretz daily said Sharon had also discussed the idea with fellow Likud party legislator Dan Meridor, who resigned the post of finance minister last month saying he had no confidence in Netanyahu.
Sharon has frequently complained that Netanyahu, 47, does not involve experienced cabinet members, including himself, in making decisions about peacemaking with the Palestinians.
Netanyahu last year became the first directly elected prime minister under reforms some in parliament assail as giving him too much power.
Currently, 61 legislators can both bring down Netanyahu and dissolve parliament at once. But 80 are needed to topple only the prime minister. Netanyahu has a 66-54 majority in parliament.
Netanyahu's cabinet secretary, Danny Naveh, called the effort to change the law "clearly anti-democratic".
"Knesset members with various political considerations want in fact to rob the voter of the choice. It's impossible", he said.

Israeli Labour party leader Ehud Barak welcomed Sharon's effort, telling army radio: "It testifies to the depth of the crisis of confidence that Netanyahu has reached with people who came to power with him."
Netanyahu passed over Sharon for the finance ministry post and a greater policymaking role to end a power struggle with Foreign Minister David Levy that threatened the government coalition.
